<!-- scenario-metadata:end -->

## Description

Verify an `animation` prop of `Stack.Screen` where a screen's
motion is written as tracks, one per animated property. Pass: each track moves
its property between its endpoints for its own duration, an omitted endpoint is
the property's rest value, a dim scrim tints the screen it is written on and
fades out with it, and an invalid track plays `default` instead. Presets used
as a screen's motion are covered by `test-stack-animation-preset-composition`.

## Note

- Wait for every transition to finish before the next tap.
- Static: the screen does not move and stays fully visible for the whole
  transition.
- "next push" applies to every screen pushed from then on; "this screen"
  changes how the current screen is popped.
- iOS: the header is not part of the screen and does not shrink, turn or dim
  with it.
- **Known issue:** iOS: the back swipe plays UIKit's own pop, whatever the
  animation (https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-screens-labs/issues/2066).

## Steps

### Baseline

1. Launch the app and navigate to the **Stack Animation Custom Motions** screen
   (on Android, launch the screen directly, see Setup).

   - [ ] "Home" is yellow with the title "Home".
   - [ ] No header is visible.
   - [ ] "next push" and "this screen" read `iosFromRight linear 2000 ms`.
   - [ ] "next push header hidden" reads `true`.
   - [ ] There is no "Pop" button.

---

### A preset rebuilt from tracks

1. Set "next push" to `iosFromRight rebuilt from tracks 2000 ms`, then tap
   "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" slides in from the right over about 2 seconds, drawn above
         "Home".
   - [ ] "Home" moves left by about a third of the width.
   - [ ] "Home" darkens slightly.
   - [ ] Both screens move at a steady speed from start to end.

2. On "Blue", tap "Pop".

   - [ ] "Blue" slides out to the right over about 2 seconds, drawn above
         "Home".
   - [ ] "Home" moves back in from the left by about a third of the width.
   - [ ] "Home" brightens while it returns.
   - [ ] Both screens move at a steady speed from start to end.

---

### Animated properties

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `from 200 left + fade 600 ms`, then tap "Push
   Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" fades in over about half a second.
   - [ ] "Blue" moves right by about half the width into place.
   - [ ] "Home" is static (see Note).

2. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `rotate + scale 2000 ms`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" grows from half its size over about 2 seconds.
   - [ ] "Blue" starts a quarter turn counterclockwise and turns clockwise
         until upright.
   - [ ] The center of "Blue" stays at the center of the screen.
   - [ ] "Home" is static.

3. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `scaleX overrides scale 2000 ms`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" starts as a band across the full width and half the screen's
         height, with its text stretched sideways.
   - [ ] Over about 2 seconds "Blue" grows taller and its text narrows, until
         "Blue" fills the screen.

---

### Dim scrim

1. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `dim blue 50% on the covered screen`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" slides in from the right over about 1 second.
   - [ ] "Home" stays in place and gradually takes a blue tint as "Blue"
         covers it: the yellow turns grayish brown and the white card lavender.
   - [ ] "Blue" keeps its own colors.

2. On "Blue", tap "Pop".

   - [ ] "Blue" slides out to the right over about 1 second.
   - [ ] The blue tint fades off "Home", which is yellow again when "Blue" is
         gone.

3. On "Home", set "next push" to `arriving screen brightens 1000 ms`, then tap
   "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" slides in from the right over about 1 second.
   - [ ] "Blue" starts almost black and brightens to its color as it arrives.
   - [ ] "Home" is static and keeps its colors.

4. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `fade out + darken 2000 ms`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] Over about 2 seconds "Home" darkens and fades out at the same time.
   - [ ] Then the whole screen is purple, not black, for about half a second.
   - [ ] Then "Blue" fades in.

---

### Per-track timing

1. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to
   `rise 2000 ms + fade 1000 ms after 1000 ms`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" rises from the bottom edge over about 2 seconds.
   - [ ] "Blue" is invisible for the first second, then fades in while still
         rising.
   - [ ] "Blue" is fully visible when it settles.

2. On "Blue", tap "Pop".

   - [ ] "Blue" moves down while fading out.
   - [ ] "Blue" is gone after about 1 second, about halfway down the screen.

3. On "Home", tap "Push Blue", on "Blue" set "this screen" to
   `hold 2000 ms on pop`, then tap "Pop".

   - [ ] "Blue" stays in place, fully visible, for about 2 seconds.
   - [ ] Then "Blue" disappears at once and "Home" is shown.

---

### Invalid values

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `invalid: no duration`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] Android: "Blue" slides in from the right only about a tenth of the
         width while fading in, and "Home" slides the same distance to the
         left.
   - [ ] iOS: "Blue" slides in from the right, and "Home" moves about a third
         of the width to the left and darkens slightly.

2. On "Blue", tap "Pop". On "Home", set "next push" to `invalid: opacity to 2`,
   then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" and "Home" move the same way as in Invalid values step 1.

3. On "Blue", tap "Pop".

   - [ ] Android: "Blue" slides about a tenth of the width to the right while
         fading out, and "Home" slides back in from the left.
   - [ ] iOS: "Blue" slides out to the right, and "Home" returns from the left
         and brightens.

## Steps - Android

### Predictive back gesture

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `rotate + scale 2000 ms`, tap "Push Blue",
   then drag from the left screen edge to the middle of the screen and hold.

   - [ ] "Blue" is turned partway clockwise, shrunk and darkened.
   - [ ] "Home" is static behind it.

2. Drag the finger back to the left screen edge and release.

   - [ ] "Blue" is upright, fills the screen and has its normal colors.

3. Drag from the left screen edge to the middle of the screen and release
   without moving it back.

   - [ ] "Blue" finishes turning clockwise, shrinking and darkening.
   - [ ] Then "Home" fills the screen.

## Steps - iOS

### Header back button

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `rotate + scale 2000 ms` and "next push header
   hidden" to `false`, then tap "Push Blue".

   - [ ] "Blue" grows and turns above a static "Home".
   - [ ] The back button and the title "Blue" fade in at the top, upright and
         in place.

2. Tap the back button in the header.

   - [ ] "Blue" shrinks, turns clockwise and darkens over about 2 seconds.
   - [ ] The back button and the title "Blue" fade out upright and in place,
         and are gone when "Blue" is.
   - [ ] "Home" is static.

---

### Back button menu

1. On "Home", set "next push" to `from 200 left + fade 600 ms`, tap "Push
   Blue", then on "Blue" tap "Push Red".

   - [ ] "Red" fades in while moving right by about half the width, above a
         static "Blue".
   - [ ] The header shows the title "Red" and a back button.

2. Touch and hold the back button in the header, then choose "Home" in the
   menu.

   - [ ] "Red" fades out while moving left by about half the width.
   - [ ] "Home" is static.
   - [ ] The back button and the title "Red" fade out in place and are gone
         when "Red" is.

---

### Hold with a header

1. On "Home", tap "Push Blue", on "Blue" set "this screen" to
   `hold 2000 ms on pop`, then tap the back button in the header.

   - [ ] "Blue" stays in place, fully visible, for about 2 seconds, then
         disappears at once.
   - [ ] The back button and the title "Blue" fade out in place over those 2
         seconds.
